PullRequest.Title: Use esbuild for local server and server-web packaging
PullRequest.Body:
## Scope

- Route local minified and non-minified `vscode-reh-*` and `vscode-reh-web-*` builds through the existing esbuild pipeline.
- Preserve codicon copying, API proposal generation, extension preparation, and the shared build date.
- Remove the redundant internal-workbench JS/CSS pair from server-web while retaining its browser shell and standalone web's direct entry.
- Leave legacy registrations and dependency removal for subsequent cleanup. No NLS runtime/cache code or tests are included here.

## Known local-build limitation (accepted)

Without #336109, switching locally built server and server-web variants at the same commit while sharing a server data directory and a non-English language pack can reuse an incompatible translated-message cache. The previous local path used a common NLS table; this migration newly exposes local builds to the target-specific table behavior that production CI already had. We are accepting that additional local-build exposure while the independent NLS fix is reviewed.

The browser/CDN table mismatch tracked in #299425 is a separate path and is not fixed or changed by this PR.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A duplicate top-level server-web entry caused the same large web workbench dependency graph and CSS graph to be bundled twice, retained in memory until post-processing, written to disk, and copied into every server-web artifact even though only the shell entry is loaded.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Every server-web core build performed redundant CPU/allocation and filesystem work and produced a larger packaged artifact containing an unused workbench JS/CSS pair.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The server-web target now emits only the browser-shell entry, allowing that one bundle to include the statically imported web workbench and eliminating one complete workbench esbuild invocation plus its redundant packaged JS/CSS outputs; standalone web retains the direct internal entry.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base server-web target included both `vs/workbench/workbench.web.main.internal` and `vs/code/browser/workbench/workbench` as independent esbuild entries. The latter statically imports the former (`src/vs/code/browser/workbench/workbench.ts:24`), while `bundle()` starts one complete esbuild build per entry with `Promise.all` and retains each output before packaging. `core-ci` invokes the server-web bundle in production pipelines, and `packageTask` copies every generated file, but the server-web HTML loads only `vs/code/browser/workbench/workbench.js`. Thus each server-web core build rebuilt and packaged an otherwise unreferenced second full workbench JS/CSS pair.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local `vscode-reh-*` and `vscode-reh-web-*` packaging, minified and non-minified
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The gulp task runs codicon/API generation, extension preparation, date generation, one esbuild child process, then the existing platform packaging task serially; all of this must complete before the local package is available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn the esbuild bundle driver (`node build/next/index.ts bundle`).
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One child process per requested local server package; internally 5 server or 16 server-web entry builds after the duplicate workbench entry is removed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The local task instead ran a full TypeScript compile/typecheck/mangle pipeline and then the legacy bundle/minify task; no esbuild child was on this local task path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The child must finish before platform packaging begins.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the HEAD commit date with `git log`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per requested local package task.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed `compileBuildWithManglingTask` already invoked the same `writeISODate('out-build')` operation once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A short synchronous subprocess runs before bundling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clean/write bundle outputs, copy curated resources, then stream all output and extensions into the platform package.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One clean/build/package traversal; file count scales with target entries, curated resources, and packaged extensions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The legacy compile/bundle/package path also cleaned and wrote core outputs and copied the resulting files and extensions; the source and implementation of the bundle pass changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the package is usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: build/gulpfile.reh.ts:670 and existing Node asset helpers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Conditionally obtain the target Node.js binary through the existing `node-${platform}-${arch}` task.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one target-node acquisition per package invocation, subject to the existing task/download behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same `serverTaskCI` and node task were already the final stage of every local server package task.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains on the packaging critical path when the asset is not locally available.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of selected bundle entry points and packaged extensions/resources; server-web has 16 effective entries after removal of the redundant internal workbench entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Top-level stages remain serialized. Inside the esbuild child, server entry builds (5) or server-web entry builds (16 after this change) run concurrently via `Promise.all`; packaging subsequently streams files. This replaces the prior full TypeScript compile followed by the legacy bundle/minify path rather than adding another pass.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Bundle output directories are deliberately cleaned, so core bundling is cold each invocation. Existing dependency/Node acquisition behavior is unchanged. The date file is overwritten once and then reused by the bundle output.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the task ordering, subprocess count, entry cardinality, and replacement behavior from the composed task definitions and bundle implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact local wall-time and peak-memory changes are unmeasured, but the new direct-source bundling replaces a repository-wide compile/typecheck and legacy bundling path; there is no evidence that it adds net work or a new scaling boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed critical path substitutes esbuild for the previous full compile plus legacy optimizer and preserves existing packaging boundaries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Production/PR `core-ci` generation of the server-web core output
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `core-ci` starts one server-web esbuild child in parallel with desktop/server builds. Within that child, every entry is independently bundled and all results are retained until NLS/source-map post-processing and writes complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the server-web esbuild bundle driver.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One child process per `core-ci` invocation; unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same server-web child process ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in parallel with other core bundles, but `core-ci` cannot complete until it finishes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build, post-process, and write each entry's JS/CSS/maps and curated resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Now 16 server-web entry builds rather than 17; one full workbench JS/CSS output pair is eliminated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both the browser shell and its statically imported web workbench were independent entries, so the large workbench graph was bundled twice and both outputs were written.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All output processing must complete before `core-ci` completes and later packaging can start.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The server-web entry count and dependency-graph size; the removed entry covered the full web workbench graph already included by the browser-shell entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One child process per target at the outer level; all entries within server-web are launched concurrently without a limiter. This PR reduces the server-web set from 17 to 16 by deleting the redundant direct workbench entry.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The target output directory is cleaned for each invocation, so there is no warm output cache or coalescing between independent entry builds.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the shell statically imports the removed entry, bundle() invokes esbuild separately for each listed entry, and production pipelines invoke `core-ci`.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timing or byte measurements are present, but duplicate graph traversal/output generation and pipeline reachability are explicit. The change is a performance fix rather than a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding against the PR. The duplicate-work removal is recorded as a regression fix tied to the introducing commit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Loading the packaged server-web browser workbench
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The HTML loads NLS modules and then only `out/vs/code/browser/workbench/workbench.js`; that shell statically contains the web workbench dependency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the server-web workbench module and its CSS/assets from the configured web base URL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One workbench JS entry request, plus its emitted CSS/assets, before and after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same shell entry was loaded and already statically bundled the internal web workbench; an additional unused internal JS/CSS pair merely existed in the package.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The shell module is on browser startup's critical path; the removed standalone internal output was off-path because the HTML never referenced it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Transferred startup bytes for the referenced shell bundle, not total artifact file count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The browser requests one workbench entry module before and after this change. The deleted standalone internal bundle was not referenced by the server-web HTML.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Normal HTTP/browser caching applies to referenced shell assets. The removed unreferenced pair had no startup cache behavior because it was not requested.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the HTML script URL and the shell's static import.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact compressed shell size is not measured, but its dependency graph is unchanged; only unreferenced packaged files are removed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No runtime startup regression. The loaded entry remains the same and the unused packaged pair is removed.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The standalone web target continues to bundle `vs/workbench/workbench.web.main.internal` directly and package it for its existing host path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the standalone web esbuild bundle driver.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One child process per standalone web build, with its existing entry set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical; the direct internal workbench entry remains in the `web` target.

Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Its entry set and esbuild scheduling are unchanged by this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing clean-build and browser cache behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the unchanged `web` branch in `getEntryPointsForTarget`.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and traced local packaging, CI core bundling, server-web startup, and standalone web. No diff-introduced performance regression met the reporting threshold. The removal of the redundant server-web workbench entry is a concrete repeated-work regression fix and was recorded separately.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
